reason: FAQ quote states an EC2 instance can be excluded from scanning by adding a resource tag with the key InspectorEc2Exclusion (value optional).
Quote states Inspector integrates with EventBridge for notification of new findings, finding state changes and suppression rule creation, and with CloudTrail for call logging.
Quote states no agent is needed, EC2 can use SSM Agent or agentless scanning when SSM Agent is not deployed, and network reachability, container image and Lambda scans need no agents.
Quote under the Classic comparison (about the new Inspector) states there is no limit to the number of instances or images that can be scanned at a time.
Under 'Can I suspend Amazon Inspector?' the quote states Inspector does not support a suspended state.
Quote states Inspector integrates with Organizations, a DA account manages it centrally and views and manages findings for all accounts in the organization.
Quote states Inspector was rearchitected and rebuilt as a new vulnerability management service, with enhancements over Inspector Classic.
Quote states all scans are event-based and workloads are scanned on discovery and rescanned; the new-CVE example is in the next context line.
Quote states the risk score is generated per finding by correlating CVE information with network reachability, exploitability data and social media trends.
Quote and its context line state the new Inspector uses SSM Agent, removing the need for a standalone Inspector agent on EC2 instances.

Quote states Inspector is an automated vulnerability management service that continually scans EC2, Lambda and container images in ECR and CI/CD tools for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
Quotes state findings are removed 24 hours after disabling Inspector and 90 days after AWS suspends the account.
Quotes state first activation enrolls the account in EC2, ECR and Lambda standard scanning, and Lambda code scanning is an optional layer that can be activated at any time.

Quotes state accounts new to Inspector get a 15-day free trial and CIS Benchmark assessments are excluded; the no-cost scanning of EC2, Lambda and ECR or code repository images is in the context sentence between them.
Quote states with Hybrid scanning agentless scans run on eligible instances every 24 hours and newly eligible instances, including ones without SSM agents, are detected and scanned every hour.
Quote states Inspector does not support scanning Lambda functions encrypted with customer managed keys, for both standard and code scanning.
Doc-history rows: Lambda code scanning added February 28, 2023 (scans developer code for vulnerabilities) and generally available June 13, 2023.
Doc-history row dated November 28, 2022 states Inspector adds support for scanning Lambda functions.
Quotes and their lines state standard scanning is the default type and scans dependencies for package vulnerabilities, code scanning scans custom code, and standard scanning must be activated first.

Quote supports a maximum of 10,000 member accounts per delegated administrator, based on Organizations quotas; but the qualifier 'not adjustable' is not stated (unlike the other rows of the table, this row has no 'You cannot request a quota increase').
Quote states verbatim that, unlike traditional scanning software, Inspector has minimal impact on fleet performance.

Quotes support no manual scheduling and automatic rescans after a new package, a patch or a new CVE; the qualifier condition 'CIS scans and Code Security use scan configurations' appears in neither quote nor context.

Quotes state only the Organizations management account can designate and remove a delegated administrator, and (under Member account actions) after activation only a delegated administrator can deactivate Inspector.
Doc-history row dated November 19, 2025 states Organizations policies automatically enable scan types across the organization and prevent unauthorized modifications.
Quote states CIS Benchmark assessment for EC2 operating systems is charged per assessment per instance.
Quote states agent-based and agentless EC2 cost is based on the average number of instances assessed in a month; proration for intermittent instances is the next context sentence.
Quote states ECR cost combines images initially scanned on push and the number of rescans per month.
Quotes under the standard and code scan paragraphs both state cost is based on the average number of Lambda functions scanned per month, prorated by coverage hours per context.

Quotes support that the score per EC2 finding correlates the CVSS base score with environment data and may be lowered when no network path to the internet exists; the qualifier condition 'package vulnerability findings' is not in the quotes or context.
Doc-history row dated June 13, 2023 states SBOM export is now available for resources Inspector scans.
Quotes state CycloneDX 1.4 and SPDX 2.3 compatible formats exported as JSON to the S3 bucket you choose, with a KMS key Inspector may use (context: to encrypt).
Quota row states a maximum of 500 saved suppression rules per account per Region and that no increase can be requested.
Doc-history row dated May 29, 2026 states the VM Scanner can be used instead of the SSM plugin for enhanced EC2 vulnerability assessments.
Doc-history row dated August 31, 2022 states Inspector can scan SSM managed Windows instances, with scans performed by the Inspector SSM plugin.

Quote supports 10 allow lists per account (1-5 predefined text, 1-5 regex), and the page intro gives per Region; but 'not adjustable' is not stated (the page says some quotas can be increased and does not say which for this one).
Doc-history row dated August 30, 2022 states allow lists specify text and text patterns Macie ignores when inspecting S3 objects.
Quote states allow lists define text and patterns Macie ignores in S3 objects, typically exceptions such as public phone numbers or sample test data.
Doc-history row dated November 28, 2022 states automated sensitive data discovery continually evaluates S3 data and samples representative objects.
Quotes state broad visibility, continual evaluation of the bucket inventory with sampling, and by default all general purpose buckets; excluding buckets is in the context line.

Quote and its line support 10,000 buckets per account for preventative control monitoring and full monitoring of the 10,000 most recent above that; 'not adjustable' is not stated (the page says some quotas can be increased).
